title: Arne Slot: Hugo Ekitike will return ‘stronger’, Alexander Isak ‘not ready’ for 90 minutes
content:
Liverpool head coach Arne Slot is hoping that Hugo Ekitike can return stronger after he ruptured his Achilles in the Champions League quarter-final against Paris Saint-Germain.

The 23-year-old is set for a long spell on the sidelines after being taken off on a stretcher in the first half. He will miss the rest of the campaign and will play no part for France in the World Cup.

Joe Gomez will also miss the Merseyside derby against Everton on Sunday through injury. The defender was a half-time substitute against PSG but was taken off after 22 minutes due to discomfort.

“He (Ekitike) hasn’t been operated on yet,” Slot told a press conference on Friday. “It is devastating for him, coming to a new club and having so much impact straight away – playing against your former club in the quarter-finals of the Champions League, with so much more to come for him in the summer

“Your first thoughts are always with him, being out for such a long time and missing out on so many special moments. He is not the first and he will not be the last player who will experience something like this at the start of his career and there are so many examples of players that have come back even stronger.

“That’s the challenge he has now and I’m 100 per cent sure he will be one of those that in 10 to 15 years time he will maybe even say this injury helped me become even stronger and even more ready to perform at an even higher level than before.“

The France international’s absence increases the spotlight on fellow No 9 Alexander Isak who started for the first time since he suffered a fractured fibula when scoring against Tottenham Hotspur in December.

The record signing has yet to make the impact expected and, while he is building match fitness, Slot admits he is not ready to play 90 minutes.

Cody Gakpo started Liverpool’s last Premier League game as their No 9 and replaced Isak up front against PSG.

“It is a good thing we have signed two No. 9s because there were a lot of people who were debating why we signed two No 9s,” Slot said. “Now all of a sudden that looks good and now people are maybe questioning if we should sign another No 9.

“Someone said to me the day after (PSG) you cannot write the script that on the day Alex is back after four months, his first start, on the same day the other one leaves the pitch with a long-term injury. But it is a good thing Alex is back now even more, although we also know he is not ready to play 90 (minutes) yet.

“There are also other players that can fill in, but those players have played in different positions throughout their life. Cody did really well when he came in. The best thing was that Hugo was still fit because two or three weeks later it would have been better because Alex is not ready for 90 yet depending on the intensity of the game. He is getting closer and closer. We need him but there are different options to play as a No 9, (Federico) Chiesa is one of them.”

Slot also provided an update on academy striker Jayden Danns, who has suffered an injury-riddled season. He last appeared for the under-21s last month, although he was forced off after 29 minutes. The 20-year-old, who has made nine senior appearances for Liverpool, “still has a lot of steps” to make.
